_comment: Every reference this manuscript cites, keyed by the name used in the prose as
[[cite:key]]. The rendered entry is generated from the registered metadata at
doi.org, never typed here: a reference list typed by hand is a list nobody
resolved. The numbering is not here either -- build_manuscript.py assigns it
from the order of first appearance, so moving a paragraph cannot leave a
citation pointing at the wrong entry.
'title' is the title as the author's own reference list carried it, before any
of this was generated. references.py fails when the registered record no
longer agrees with it. That is the whole value of the field: copying the
registered title in here would verify nothing. It is required for every
reference, so that no title reaches the page without having been compared
On the first run this caught one: Crossref registers Radiology 2011;259(2) as
'They AreNotthe Same Thing', having lost the spaces around the italicised
An entry with 'literal' instead of 'doi' is not registered anywhere: the reason
is recorded with it, because an unresolvable reference is otherwise

references.reason: A NEA-OECD workshop report with no registered DOI. Checked at doi.org and at Crossref by title on 2026-11-07; neither carries it. The photon cross-section database this work generates its material files from is the one distributed with this report, so the reference is the primary source and cannot be replaced by a later paper.

references.note: Added 2026-11-07. The nearest published work to this one: it measures how far three organ-dose packages disagree under identical scan conditions and attributes the spread to phantom anatomy and size rather than to inaccuracy. That is the same mechanism this paper bounds from the other side, so it is the comparator the Discussion needs.
